title: A clearing-free protocol for imaging intact whole adipose tissue innervation in mice
protocol: Euthanize mouse following general euthanasia protocol.
Excise intact axillary subcutaneous white adipose tissue from the mouse.
Excise intact inguinal subcutaneous white adipose tissue from the mouse.
Maintain orientation of inguinal scWAT for all future steps.
Note whether the tissue was taken from mouse-left or mouse-right side.
Place mouse ventral side up.
Spray the mouse with 70% EtOH.
Make a central incision from the base of the tail extending to the top of the sternum, being sure not to penetrate the underlying peritoneal cavity.
Gently use forceps and thumbs to pull ventral skin away from both flanks, pulling slowly with even pressure.
Cut the large vasculature leading to the inguinal scWAT depot.
Trace the edges of the inguinal scWAT depot using scissors.
Use forceps to gently roll the adipose tissue away from the skin.
Weigh the inguinal scWAT depot and place it into a 6-well plate with 3–5 mL ice-cold 2% PFA.
Fix the inguinal scWAT depot at 4°C without agitation for 8 hours if ≤0.08g, or for 16-24 hours if >0.08g.
Identify the axillary scWAT depot underneath both forelimbs.
Use forceps to pull away a thin muscle layer enveloping the dorsolateral portion of each axillary depot.
Trace the edges of the axillary scWAT depot using scissors.
Use forceps to gently roll the adipose tissue away from the skin, cutting anchoring connective tissue as necessary.
Weigh the freed adipose tissue depot.
Place the weighed tissue into a 6-well plate containing 3-5 mL of ice-cold 2% PFA.
Fix the tissue at 4°C without agitation for ≤0.08g for 8 hours or >0.08g for 16-24 hours.
Aspirate PFA from each well and add 1× PBS with heparin.
Wash tissues in 1× PBS with heparin on an orbital shaker at 4°C for one hour, replacing the buffer after 30 minutes.
Pause the protocol after completing any series of 1× PBS washes.
Use forceps to place the tissue flat onto the center of a large glass slide.
Add 2–3 drops of PBS onto the tissue using a transfer pipette.
Place a second large glass slide on top of the tissue, sandwiching it between the two slides.
Clamp the slides together with two large binder clips.
Allow tissues to remain compressed for 1 hour and 30 minutes at 4°C.
Mount each piece of tissue onto a concave slide.
Place the mounted tissues into a 6-well plate with 3-5 mL blocking buffer at 4°C for 16-24 hours.
Exchange fresh blocking buffer daily during the blocking and permeabilization period for larger tissues (>0.30 g) extended to 3 days.
Perform autofluorescence quenching using typogen black or an alternative method if specified.
Incubate tissues in 0.1% typogen black for 20 minutes at approximately 20°C.
Wash the tissue in 1× PBS for 4 hours at approximately 20°C, replacing PBS every 1 hour.
Incubate tissues in 1× TrueBlack® Lipofuscin Autofluorescence Quencher for 10 minutes at approximately 20°C.
Wash the tissue in 1× PBS for 4 hours at 4°C, replacing PBS every 1 hour.
Prepare a fresh working solution for injection by mixing components 30 minutes before each injection time point.
Stepwise dehydrate samples in methanol diluted in PBS at approximately 50% MeOH for 1 hour, then increase to 80% and finally to 100%, replacing fresh after the first hour.
Bleach samples in 5% H2O2 mixed with 20% DMSO/MeOH for 16–24 hours at 4°C.
Rehydrate samples by gradually decreasing methanol concentration from 100% to 80%, then to 50%, and finally in PBS, replacing fresh after the first hour of each step.
Perform all future steps at approximately 20°C to reduce autofluorescence and non-specific binding.
Wash tissues in 1× PBS containing heparin if desired to further reduce vascular autofluorescence.
Add sodium azide at a concentration of 0.02% to PBS for all future washes to prevent microbial growth.
Avoid adding non-ionic detergents such as Triton X-100 or Tween 20 when using typogen black or TrueBlack autofluorescence quenching.
Follow the order outlined below for co-staining with primary and secondary antibodies, isolectin-IB4, and DAPI to reduce non-specific binding and cross-reactivity.
Boost endogenous signal with a fluorophore conjugated antibody against the fluorescent protein of interest immediately after completing step 9.
Dilute desired primary antibody in 1× PBS for use in the protocol.
For antibodies not validated in this protocol, perform an antibody titration to find optimal dilution.
Start antibody titration with concentrations that work well for thin sections.
Concentrating the optimized concentration by two-fold typically results in better staining outcomes.
Incubate tissues in primary antibody solution for 2 days at 4°C.
Wash tissues in 1× PBS for 4 hours at 4°C, replacing PBS every 1 hour.
Dilute the desired secondary antibody in 1× PBS if not using a directly conjugated primary antibody.
Incubate tissues in secondary antibody solution for 16–24 hours at 4°C.
Wash tissues in 1× PBS for 4 hours at 4°C, replacing PBS every 1 hour.
Make Isolectin-IB4 working solution as described in materials and equipment.
Allow Isolectin-IB4 working solution to warm to ∼20°C if not already.
Add 3–5 mL of Isolectin-IB4 working solution to each tissue and incubate for 16–24 hours at ∼20°C.
Wash tissues in 1× PBS for 2 hours at ∼20°C, replacing PBS every hour.
Dilute Isolectin-IB4 working solution to 1 μg/mL if necessary.
Incubate tissues in 3–5 mL DAPI working solution for 1 hour at ∼20°C.
Wash tissues in 1× PBS for 2 hours at ∼20°C, replacing PBS after 1 hour.
Label the top of a large glass slide with mouse and tissue identifying information.
Remove tissue from 6-well plate and place it at the center of the large glass slide.
Add a generous amount (4–6 drops) of glycerol-based mounting fluid to the tissue.
Place a large (48 × 60 mm) glass coverslip over the tissue.
Apply gentle pressure to the coverslip to help it adhere to the tissue and slide.
Place the coverslipped slides underneath uniform weight (15–20 kg) for 3 days.
Remove the slide from underneath the textbooks after 3 days.
Seal the edges with nail polish.
Mount whole axillary and inguinal scWAT depots fully and seal them following immunostaining.
Place the tissues medial side up with the anterior portion closest to the label.
Let dry for 5 minutes.
Proceed to imaging.
Imaging can be performed within a week after mounting is complete.
Capture images using widefield epifluorescence microscopy.
Use magnifications of up to 40× objectives for easy image capture on widefield microscopes.
